plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small deciduous tree that produces fragrant, five-petaled blossoms on bare branches in the depths of winter. It is widely cultivated in East Asia and prized for both its ornamental flowers and its tart fruit used in pickling and liqueurs.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (January to March)
plants.location: China, Japan, Korea; cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms are a symbol of perseverance in East Asian culture because they bloom while snow may still be on the ground.

plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: A small bulbous perennial with nodding, bell-shaped white flowers marked with green on the inner petals. It naturalizes in woodlands and gardens, often pushing up through frost and snow.
plants.location: Europe, from the Pyrenees to Ukraine; naturalized in the UK and North America
plants.funFact: Snowdrops contain galantamine, a compound that has been developed into a medication used to treat symptoms of Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Hamamelis x intermedia
plants.description: A large deciduous shrub with spidery, ribbon-like petals that appear on leafless branches and emit a spicy fragrance. Many cultivars are grown in temperate gardens for winter interest.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-winter to early spring (January to March)
plants.location: Hybrid of Asian species; cultivated across Europe and North America
plants.funFact: The petals curl up tightly in freezing weather to protect themselves and then unfurl when temperatures rise.

plants.name: Delonix regia
plants.description: A broad, umbrella-shaped tropical tree that becomes covered in clusters of vivid blooms. In some regions it blooms in the warm season, which in the Southern Hemisphere includes February.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer in the Southern Hemisphere (December to March); spring to summer in the northern tropics
plants.location: Native to Madagascar; widely planted in tropical and subtropical regions including Australia, Brazil, and South Africa
plants.funFact: Although it is famous worldwide, the Flame Tree is endangered in its native Madagascar habitat.
